prs.title: fix: terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown
prs.author: weiguangli-io
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE connections (the per-request POST stream and the standalone GET stream) are not gracefully closed when a session is terminated or the session manager shuts down, so their EventSourceResponse coroutines get cancelled mid-stream instead of completing, which surfaces as Uvicorn ASGI-incomplete-response errors/hangs on shutdown. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE connections (the per-request POST stream and the standalone GET stream) are not gracefully closed when a session is terminated or the session manager shuts down, so their EventSourceResponse coroutines get cancelled mid-stream instead of completing, which surfaces as Uvicorn ASGI-incomplete-response errors/hangs on shutdown. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2253 is the complete two-file change: it adds the loop in streamable_http.py's terminate() that closes every writer in self._sse_stream_writers, and wires the trigger by editing streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan to call session termination before cancelling tasks on shutdown. #3218 only touches streamable_http.py to register the GET-stream writer into self._sse_stream_writers (its own added comment notes it relies on 'terminate()/close_sse_stream()' already being able to close the writer), so on its own it lacks the manager-level shutdown sequencing needed to actually invoke termination — it's the narrower half of the same fix and its registration change should be folded into #2253 rather than merged separately.

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch pre_parse_json's decision of when to skip JSON-parsing a string value, targeting the same bug: fields typed as a union involving `str` (most notably `str | None`) get their string value incorrectly run through json.loads, corrupting valid string payloads that happen to look like JSON. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch pre_parse_json's decision of when to skip JSON-parsing a string value, targeting the same bug: fields typed as a union involving `str` (most notably `str | None`) get their string value incorrectly run through json.loads, corrupting valid string payloads that happen to look like JSON. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 unwraps `Annotated[...]` before comparing union members against `str` via its `_unwrap_annotated`/`_is_optional_str` helpers, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` without unwrapping Annotated, so a union member like `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` never matches the simple-types frozenset and the fix silently fails to trigger for Field-annotated optional-str parameters. #2032 is also broader in scope (skips pre-parsing for any all-simple-type union, e.g. `str | int`), which changes pre-parsing behavior beyond the reported bug rather than the minimal, targeted `str | None` fix in #3056.

prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address the same routing-key collision: `_request_streams` is keyed by request id with no duplicate check, so two concurrent requests sharing an id silently overwrite each other's stream slot and cross-wire responses. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address the same routing-key collision: `_request_streams` is keyed by request id with no duplicate check, so two concurrent requests sharing an id silently overwrite each other's stream slot and cross-wire responses. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 detects the duplicate but keys off the pre-existing `str(message.id)` conversion, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids (int `1` and string `"1"`) into one dict key — so it still cross-wires mixed int/str ids and its key namespace can collide with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 replaces the stringification with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that type-tags keys (`i:`/`s:`) so int/string ids never collide, and explicitly guards the `GET_STREAM_KEY` collision — a strict superset fix for the same underlying problem.

members.author: wiggzz

members.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 detects the duplicate but keys off the pre-existing `str(message.id)` conversion, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids (int `1` and string `"1"`) into one dict key — so it still cross-wires mixed int/str ids and its key namespace can collide with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 replaces the stringification with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that type-tags keys (`i:`/`s:`) so int/string ids never collide, and explicitly guards the `GET_STREAM_KEY` collision — a strict superset fix for the same underlying problem.
